## Dropship for SteamOS 0.1.4

A correction to 0.1.3, which tried to fix the *Dropship for SteamOS is not responding* dialog at
shutdown and did not manage it. If you are on 0.1.3, this one is worth taking; if you are on 0.1.2
or earlier, read this as the fix for that dialog.

### Fixed in this release

- **0.1.3 noticed a stalled window and left it too late to help.** The mechanism it added was right
  and it did run — the journal from the Deck shows the app leaving by itself — but it waited twenty
  seconds, and twenty seconds is longer than the desktop's patience. What the journal shows, to the
  second: the app stranded a frame at 23:41:53, the shutdown began at 23:42:13, and the app left at
  23:42:13, i.e. at the exact moment the desktop began asking windows to close. The dialog appeared
  anyway. Leaving only helps if it happens while you are still deciding to power off.

  0.1.4 leaves five seconds after the window stops being drawn. That is several missed requests —
  Dropship asks itself for a fresh frame every two seconds even when nothing has changed — so a
  window that is working never looks quiet for anything close to it.

  A window that has never drawn anything at all still gets twenty seconds, because the first frame
  is the expensive one: graphics context, shader compilation, and on a cold start that is seconds
  rather than milliseconds. A slow start is not a stall and must not be treated as one.

### What you should know

- The trade is unchanged in kind and larger in degree: if the window stops being drawn for five
  seconds, Dropship closes itself. A window that cannot draw is of no use, and the stalls recorded
  on real hardware never recovered — one was still frozen two minutes after becoming visible again
  — so this is the better of the two outcomes rather than a compromise.
- The stall that triggered this was **not** a game. In that session no game was running at all;
  something in the desktop covered the window for long enough to strand a frame. So this is not
  only a gaming-session problem, and the shorter timeout is not only about games.

### Verified on a real Steam Deck

With the app hosted by a throwaway compositor, and the kill stop/resume trick standing in for the
display going away:

- a healthy window left alone for 60 seconds is still running;
- a stall that ends by itself in 3 seconds is survived;
- a stall that never ends is left at 7 seconds, with *"The window has not been drawn for 5s, which
  means the display has stopped answering it; leaving rather than hanging."* in the journal.

Also verified in the real desktop session, which is the one that matters for the threshold: the
app ran healthy for 60 seconds with its event loop in `epoll_wait` and no watchdog message. Its
CPU accounting over that minute shows it painting about every two seconds, each frame costing
around a millisecond — which is the margin five seconds is built on, and it holds in the session
the app actually runs in, not only in the test rig.

The stall in the journal was triggered by something specific to that moment, and this release does
not claim to have found it — it claims to be gone soon enough afterwards.

### Not yet verified

The same thing 0.1.3 could not verify, and the one that counts: install this, play or work until a
window has covered Dropship, then power off. The evidence says the app is now gone well before the
shutdown asks about it, but only a real shutdown shows whether the dialog is gone with it.

If the dialog does appear again, the journal line *"The window has not been drawn for Ns…"* settles
what happened: if it is there, the app saw the stall and left, and the desktop was already asking;
if it is absent, the window stopped responding in some way the watchdog does not see, which is a
different bug and the next thing to chase.

### Install

```sh
tar -xzf dropship-steamos-0.1.4-linux-x86_64.tar.gz
cd dropship-steamos-0.1.4
sha256sum -c SHA256SUMS
sudo ./install.sh
```

That installs the privileged helper, the watcher service and a **Dropship for SteamOS** entry in
the application launcher. Open it, choose your regions, and switch on **Block while Overwatch
runs**. Remove everything again with `sudo ./install.sh --uninstall`.

If you already have an earlier version installed, running the same commands upgrades it in place;
there is no separate upgrade step, and your region selection is left alone.

Requires x86_64 SteamOS. Built on Ubuntu 24.04, which is older than the Deck's glibc — so nothing
newer than what the Deck already has is required. The binaries are dynamically linked against
glibc, so they are not portable to musl distributions.
